colophon: First Part — the Wave of Bliss.

lines.1: On the earth, for those whose feet have stumbled, the earth itself becomes the support;
lines.2: for those who have offended against you, you alone, O auspicious one, are the refuge.
lines.3: Shiva, when united with Shakti, becomes able to bring forth creation;
lines.4: without her, the god cannot even stir.
lines.5: Therefore, you whom even Hari, Hara, and Virinchi themselves must worship —
lines.6: how could one lacking merit from a former life ever manage to bow to you, or sing your praise?
lines.7: Gathering the finest dust that falls from your lotus feet,
lines.8: Brahma the creator fashions the worlds, each one flawless.
lines.9: Vishnu bears that same dust, with some effort, upon his thousand heads,
lines.10: and Shiva grinds it fine and smears it over his body as sacred ash.
lines.11: That dust is a sunlit city dispelling the deep darkness at the far end of ignorance,
lines.12: a stream of honeyed nectar flowing from clustered blossoms of awareness for those who are inert,
lines.13: a string of wish-granting gems for the poor,
lines.14: and, for those sinking in the ocean of birth, the tusk of Vishnu's boar form that lifts them out.
lines.15: Every other deity holds up both hands in the gestures of fearlessness and boon-granting;
lines.16: you alone show no such display.
lines.17: To rescue from fear, and to grant fruit greater even than what is wished for,
lines.18: O shelter of all the worlds, your two feet alone are enough.
lines.19: Vishnu, worshipping you, mother of good fortune to all who bow before you,
lines.20: once took the form of a woman and stirred even Shiva, destroyer of the triple city.
lines.21: And Kama too, bowing to you, gained a form for Rati's eyes to drink in —
lines.22: a form that still overwhelms the hearts of even the greatest sages with longing.
lines.23: A bow strung with flowers, its cord a line of bees, five blossoms for arrows,
lines.24: spring as his ally, the sandal-breeze off the Malaya hills as his chariot —
lines.25: with just this, O daughter of the snowy mountain, and one glance of compassion caught from the corner of your eye,
lines.26: the bodiless god of love conquers this entire world.
lines.27: With a girdle of chiming bells, bent low beneath breasts like a young elephant's frontal lobes,
lines.28: slender at the waist, her face like the full autumn moon,
lines.29: holding in her hands bow and arrows, noose and goad —
lines.30: may that very embodiment of the pride of Shiva, destroyer of the triple city, stand before us.
lines.31: In the middle of the ocean of nectar, ringed by a grove of wish-granting heavenly trees,
lines.32: on the island of gems, amid a garden of kadamba trees, within a house built of wish-fulfilling jewels,
lines.33: upon a couch shaped like Shiva, reclining on the bed that is the Supreme Shiva himself —
lines.34: there, only a rare few, truly blessed, worship you, the very wave of consciousness and bliss.
lines.35: Earth in the root center, a certain seed in the navel center, fire seated in the center below the navel,
lines.36: air in the heart, space above that, and even mind at the point between the brows —
lines.37: piercing through the whole hidden path in this way,
lines.38: you sport in secret with your lord in the thousand-petaled lotus at the crown.
lines.39: Showering all creation with streams of nectar flowing down between your two feet,
lines.40: you pour that radiance, drawn from the deepest source, over the whole world once more,
lines.41: then, reaching your own ground, coiled three and a half times like a serpent,
lines.42: you gather yourself into yourself and sleep in the hidden cavity of the root center.
lines.43: Formed of four triangles that are Shiva and five that are Shakti,
lines.44: nine distinct triangles together making up your own true ground,
lines.45: these forty-four corners, together with the two ringed lotuses, the three encircling lines and three circles,
lines.46: come together as the corners of your citadel, the Sri Chakra.
lines.47: To measure your beauty, O daughter of the snow-capped mountain,
lines.48: even the greatest poets, Brahma among them, can scarcely make the attempt —
lines.49: a beauty so longed-for that celestial women, merely to glimpse it, reach in their minds
lines.50: a state of union with Shiva that even long austerity could hardly attain.
lines.51: An old man, unpleasant to look at, dull in wit and humor —
lines.52: once he falls beneath your sidelong glance, hundreds of young women run after him,
lines.53: their braids coming undone, the cloth slipping from their full breasts,
lines.54: their girdle-strings snapping loose, their fine robes falling away.
lines.55: Fifty-six rays shine in the realm of earth, fifty-two in the realm of water,
lines.56: sixty-two in fire, fifty-four in the wind,
lines.57: seventy-two in space, and sixty-four in the mind —
lines.58: and above all of these countless rays rests the pair of your lotus feet.
lines.59: Pure as autumn moonlight, crowned with matted locks that bear the crescent moon,
lines.60: your hands showing the signs of boon-giving and protection while holding a crystal rosary and a book —
lines.61: without bowing to you even once, how could the speech of the wise ever come to hold
lines.62: a sweetness surpassing that of honey, milk, and grapes?
lines.63: Those rare, good souls who worship you as the ruddy dawn-light,
lines.64: the first sunlight falling on the lotus-grove of poets' hearts,
lines.65: delight the wise with speech as deep and fresh as the very waves
lines.66: of passion belonging to Saraswati, the beloved of Brahma.
lines.67: Whoever meditates on you together with Vashini and the other mother-goddesses of speech,
lines.68: radiant as fragments of moonstone, O mother —
lines.69: that person becomes a maker of great poems,
lines.70: their words graceful, sweet as the very fragrance breathed from the lotus-mouth of the goddess of speech.
lines.71: Whoever contemplates the whole sky and earth immersed in the crimson glow of your body,
lines.72: a glow like that of the young rising sun —
lines.73: for him, countless heavenly courtesans, their eyes shy as startled forest deer,
lines.74: along with Urvashi herself, come under his spell.
lines.75: Whoever meditates on your form as the seed of desire — your face as the central point,
lines.76: your two breasts below it, and beneath them the triangle that is Hara's half, O queen of Hara —
lines.77: he can, with the greatest ease, stir any woman to passion at once,
lines.78: indeed he can set the whole triple world trembling, sun and moon its very breasts.
lines.79: Whoever holds you in his heart, streaming from your limbs a nectar-light like moonbeams,
lines.80: as though you were a form carved from moonstone —
lines.81: that person, like Garuda, subdues the pride of serpents,
lines.82: and with a glance alone, a stream of nectar, soothes those burning with fever.
lines.83: Slender as a streak of lightning, formed of sun, moon, and fire,
lines.84: seated above all six lotus centers —
lines.85: the great ones, their minds scoured clean of all impurity and delusion, who behold this subtle form of yours in the grove of the thousand-petaled lotus,
lines.86: hold within themselves waves of the highest bliss.
lines.87: Whoever, wishing to say, 'Bhavani, cast your compassionate glance on me, your servant,'
lines.88: manages only to utter, 'Bhavani, you...' before the words fail him —
lines.89: to him you grant, then and there, the very state of union with yourself,
lines.90: a state whose feet are honored with waving lamps by the bright crowns of Vishnu, Brahma, and Indra.
lines.91: Not content, it seems, with taking merely the left half of Shiva's body for your own,
lines.92: I suspect you, with a mind still unsatisfied, took his other half as well —
lines.93: for this whole form of yours glows reddish and bears three eyes,
lines.94: bent low beneath your breasts, its crown set with the curved crescent moon.
lines.95: Brahma brings the world forth, Vishnu preserves it, Rudra dissolves it,
lines.96: and Ishvara, concealing even his own form, withdraws it from view —
lines.97: while Sadashiva, ever present before all these, graciously sanctions each of these acts,
lines.98: acting only on the command carried in the barest flicker of your eyebrow-creepers.
lines.99: O auspicious one, worship offered to your two feet
lines.100: becomes, in itself, worship of the three gods born from the three qualities of nature —
lines.101: for near the very jeweled pedestal on which your feet rest,
lines.102: these three stand always, their joined palms held above their heads like crowns.
lines.103: In the great dissolution, Brahma himself passes away, Vishnu ceases to be,
lines.104: Yama, lord of death, perishes, and Kubera, lord of wealth, meets his end,
lines.105: even the tireless ranks of Indra close their eyes and are gone —
lines.106: only your husband, O auspicious one, remains, still at play through it all.
lines.107: May my muttering become your mantra, my talk become prayer, all my handiwork become the shaping of sacred gestures,
lines.108: my walking become circling round you, and my eating and all such acts become an offering into your fire,
lines.109: my lying down become prostration, and — seen through the eye of complete self-surrender —
lines.110: may every pleasure of mine become, in its turn, an act of worship to you.
lines.111: All the gods, Brahma, Indra, and the rest, though they taste the nectar that wards off dreadful old age and death,
lines.113: But time itself has no hold on Shiva, who once swallowed the terrible poison —
lines.114: and the true source of that is not the nectar he drank, but the glory of your earring, O mother.
lines.115: 'Move aside from Brahma's crown ahead of you!'
lines.116: 'Careful, you will stumble on Vishnu's hard crown — kick Indra's crown out of the way!'
lines.117: When you suddenly arrive at Shiva's hall as all these gods bow low before you,
lines.118: and Shiva himself rises to greet you — glorious indeed are the cries of your attendants, clearing your path.
lines.119: Whoever meditates always, 'I am you,' upon you, the eternal one,
lines.120: surrounded on every side by radiant powers such as the gift of becoming infinitesimal — powers born from your own body —
lines.121: what wonder is it if that person comes to regard even Shiva's three-eyed splendor as mere grass,
lines.122: while the very fire that consumes the universe at the end of time performs the lamp-waving rite in his honor?
lines.123: Having first taught the world sixty-four other tantras,
lines.124: each one devoted only to some particular, limited attainment, Pashupati stood content with that —
lines.125: until, at your urging, he brought down to this earth one further, self-sufficient tantra,
lines.126: one that alone secures the whole, complete fourfold goal of human life.
lines.127: Shiva, Shakti, desire, earth, the sun, the cool-rayed moon,
lines.128: the god of love, the swan-syllable, Indra, and then the syllables of Para, Mara, and Hari —
lines.129: these, joined at their three endings with the seed-syllable Hrim,
lines.130: come together, O mother, as the very letters that spell your sacred name.
lines.131: Placing at the head of the mantra these three seed-syllables — of desire, of origin, and of fortune —
lines.132: some devotees, ever intent on boundless, exalted enjoyment,
lines.133: worship you, the eternal one, their rosary strung with wish-fulfilling gems,
lines.134: pouring hundreds of oblations of fragrant ghee as streams into the fire that is Shiva.
lines.135: You are the very body of Shambhu, your two breasts the sun and moon;
lines.136: and I take your own self, O blessed one, to be the flawless Navatman, the ninefold form of Shiva himself.
lines.137: Being thus, each to the other, both substance and possessor of that substance,
lines.138: the bond between you two, both absorbed in the very same supreme bliss, is one of complete, indivisible unity.
lines.139: You are mind, you are space, you are air, you are fire, the charioteer of the wind;
lines.140: you are water, you are earth — and once you have become all of this, nothing at all remains beyond you.
lines.141: It is you alone who, in order to unfold your own self into the shape of this whole universe,
lines.142: carry, O youthful consort of Shiva, the very form of consciousness and bliss.
lines.143: I bow to the supreme Shambhu, seated in the command-center between the brows,
lines.144: blazing with the light of a million suns and moons, joined always at his side by you, the Supreme Consciousness.
lines.145: Whoever worships him with devotion comes to dwell in that realm beyond all ordinary light,
lines.146: a realm untouched by sun, moon, or fire, yet itself lit from within.
lines.147: In the throat center, I worship Shiva, clear as pure crystal, the very source of space,
lines.148: together with the goddess who shares his nature equally —
lines.149: by whose combined radiance, spreading like moonlight along its path,
lines.150: the world, its inner darkness driven off, shines like a chakora bird rejoicing in the moon.
lines.151: I worship that indescribable pair of swans, roaming freely in the minds of the great,
lines.152: forever savoring the nectar of the freshly blossoming lotus of awareness —
lines.153: from whose soft murmuring comes the fulfillment of all eighteen branches of learning,
lines.154: and which, like swans straining milk from water, draw out only what is good, leaving every fault behind.
lines.155: In your center below the navel, O mother, I praise the ever-burning fire seated there,
lines.156: the great fire of universal dissolution, together with the great lord who shares your rites —
lines.157: whose gaze, when kindled with great anger, burns up entire worlds,
lines.158: yet whose glance, melted with compassion, becomes instead a cooling balm.
lines.159: I worship the dark, cloud-like presence seated in your navel center,
lines.160: flashing with lightning that is your own power dispelling darkness, wrapped in a shimmering rainbow of jewels,
lines.161: a cloud that alone shelters this world,
lines.162: raining down to cool all three worlds scorched by the fierce sun of Hara's wrath.
lines.163: In your root center, I meditate on the ninefold Shiva as the great dancer,
lines.164: performing the fierce tandava of the nine sentiments, together with you, absorbed in the graceful dance of lasya.
lines.165: From these two, moved by compassion, joined together for the sake of creation,
lines.166: this whole world was born, having both a father and a mother.
lines.167: Second Part — the Wave of Beauty.
lines.168: Whoever praises your golden crown, O daughter of the snow-mountain,
lines.169: thick-set with sky-jewels that have themselves turned to rubies in its light —
lines.170: why should his mind not also see, in the shimmering, many-hued crescent moon it bears,
lines.171: a likeness to Indra's own rainbow bow?
lines.172: May your mass of hair, dense, glossy, and soft as a whole forest of freshly opened blue lotuses,
lines.173: dispel the darkness that surrounds us, O auspicious one —
lines.174: hair so naturally fragrant that, I imagine,
lines.175: the very trees of Indra's own garden come to dwell within it, just to catch its scent.
lines.176: May the parting of your hair grant us well-being —
lines.177: a line like the very channel carrying off the overflowing tide of beauty from your face,
lines.178: bearing along it a streak of vermilion, as though
lines.179: it held captive, deep within your heavy dark tresses, a ray of the fresh morning sun.
lines.180: Your face, framed by naturally curling locks as graceful as young bees,
lines.181: outshines and mocks the beauty of even the lotus.
lines.182: On that face, softly smiling, lovely with the pollen-glow of your teeth,
lines.183: fragrant bees — the very eyes of the fire that once burned Kama — hover about, intoxicated.
lines.184: Your forehead shines, pure with the radiance of your own beauty;
lines.185: I take it to be a second crescent moon, alongside the one set in your crown.
lines.186: When the two, facing each other, come together as one,
lines.187: joined as though sealed with nectar, they merge into a single, full moon.
lines.188: O you who delight in dispelling the fear of the whole world,
lines.189: your two eyebrows, gently curved, joined by your two bee-dark eyes as its string —
lines.190: I take these together as the bow of the god of love, held in his right hand,
lines.191: its hidden middle concealed, O Uma, between wrist and closed fist.
lines.192: Your right eye, being of the nature of the sun, brings forth the day;
lines.193: your left eye, being of the nature of the moon, brings forth the night;
lines.194: and your third eye, glowing like a half-opened golden lotus,
lines.195: brings forth the twilight that moves between the two, day and night.
lines.196: Your glance is vast, auspicious, and clear in its splendor — unconquerable, one might say, amid a field of blue lotuses,
lines.197: the very bed on which compassion flows, sweet beyond telling, a haven of its own,
lines.198: surpassing, in its glory, the greatness of many famous cities —
lines.199: it fittingly bears, in truth, every one of their names, and shines forth triumphant.
lines.200: Your two ears are like a pair of young bees, ever intent on tasting the nectar-cluster of poets' finest phrases,
lines.201: casting sidelong glances toward your restless eyes and never quite letting them go —
lines.202: and Shiva's forehead-eye, watching these two eyes so eager, tasting every fresh delight,
lines.203: grows faintly red with jealousy at the sight.
lines.204: Melting with tenderness when turned toward Shiva, scornful of everyone else,
lines.205: flaring with jealousy at the sight of the Ganga, filled with wonder at the deeds of Shiva,
lines.206: fearful before Shiva's serpents, the very source of the lotus's own beauty,
lines.207: smiling among your companions — O mother, let that same glance of yours turn compassionate on me too.
lines.208: O crest-jewel bud of the mountain-lord's own line,
lines.209: your two eyes, their lashes reaching almost to your ears like feathers on an arrow,
lines.210: enact between them the very play of Kama's arrow, drawn back to the ear,
lines.211: an arrow whose one aim is to shatter the tranquil calm of Shiva's mind.
lines.212: O beloved of Ishana, your three eyes, each distinctly colored,
lines.213: yet blended together by the playful touch of collyrium, shine as one —
lines.214: as if bearing within them the three qualities of nature — passion, clarity, and inertia —
lines.215: ready to create anew Brahma, Vishnu, and Rudra, should these gods ever cease to be.
lines.216: O you whose heart belongs wholly to Pashupati,
lines.217: with your three eyes, companions of compassion, glowing red, white, and dark,
lines.218: you bring to us — surely as the red river Shona, the Ganga, and the dark Yamuna, daughter of the sun —
lines.219: the very meeting-point of three sacred rivers, to cleanse us and make us pure.
lines.220: O daughter of the king of mountains, the wise say that this whole world
lines.221: passes into dissolution and springs back into being through the mere closing and opening of your eyes.
lines.222: This entire world, having been born of your eyes' opening,
lines.223: I suspect your eyes now refuse to close at all, simply to shield it from dissolving again.
lines.224: O Aparna, the little fish, fearful of the whispering malice carried by your eyes that reach almost to your ears,
lines.225: hide themselves constantly, unblinking, in the water,
lines.226: and that same beauty, the goddess dwelling in the lotus, shuts fast the doors of the blue lotus's petals at dusk,
lines.227: only to prise them open and slip inside again each dawn.
lines.228: O auspicious one, let your long, compassionate glance — radiant as a half-opened blue lotus —
lines.229: bathe even me, distant and wretched though I am.
lines.230: By this I am made blessed, and you lose nothing by it,
lines.231: for the moon lets its rays fall equally on the forest and on the palace.
lines.232: O daughter of the mountain-king, whose mind is not captivated
lines.233: by the graceful curve of your two eye-corners, a fascination like Kama's own flower-bow?
lines.234: There, where your sidelong glance slants past the edge of your ear and lingers, playing,
lines.235: it seems poised exactly as an arrow being fitted to its string.
lines.236: I take this face of yours, its two earrings mirrored in your glowing cheeks,
lines.237: to be a four-wheeled chariot belonging to the god of love —
lines.238: mounted on which the great warrior Kama wages his war
lines.239: against Shiva, lord of the ghostly hosts, who himself rides a chariot of the whole earth, its wheels the sun and moon.
lines.240: As you drink in, cupped in your ears, the skillful, nectar-like waves of Saraswati's fine words,
lines.242: the cluster of your earrings, swaying as your head nods in astonished delight,
lines.243: seems, with its own ringing jingle, to be answering her back in reply.
lines.244: May this ridge of your nose — banner-flag of the whole snow-mountain lineage —
lines.245: quickly grant us the fruit that is rightly ours,
lines.246: a nose that carries, moistened by the cool overflow of your own breath, pearls within it,
lines.247: and, from the very abundance of those pearls, wears a string of pearls outside it as well.
lines.248: O you of lovely teeth, let me venture just one comparison for the natural red glow of your lip —
lines.249: let it be the coral vine, and may that comparison bear fruit.
lines.250: As for the red bimba fruit — reddened, in truth, only by reflecting your lip's own color —
lines.251: how could it not feel ashamed to be weighed against it, even in the smallest degree?
lines.252: From drinking too deeply of the net of moonlight cast by your smiling, moon-like face,
lines.253: the chakora birds' beaks have gone numb with the sheer excess of its sweetness.
lines.254: That is why, their taste soured now, they turn instead to the rays of the ordinary moon,
lines.255: drinking them freely, night after night, mistaking that nectar for nothing more than sour gruel.
lines.256: Your tongue triumphs, O mother, tirelessly repeating again and again the praise of your lord's own virtues,
lines.258: and Saraswati, whose own form is like clear, transparent crystal, seated at its very tip,
lines.259: herself takes on there the glowing hue of ruby.
lines.260: Skanda, Indra, and Vishnu, mighty warriors returning triumphant from battle against the demons,
lines.261: their armor still on though their helmets are lost, too reverent even to touch what belongs to Shiva himself —
lines.262: these three alone are given, O mother, camphor-white and moon-bright,
lines.263: the melting remnants of betel-leaf left over from your own mouth.
lines.264: When you take up the lute and begin to sing the many heroic deeds of Pashupati,
lines.265: nodding your head as you praise each fine phrase —
lines.266: Saraswati, her own lute's gentle music put utterly to shame by the sweetness of your voice,
lines.267: quietly wraps her instrument in cloth and falls silent.
lines.268: Touched gently by your father's fingertips, the snow-mountain himself, out of sheer affection,
lines.269: lifted again and again by Shiva, eager to drink from your lips,
lines.270: held in his hand as though it were the very stem of the mirror that is his own face —
lines.271: how, O daughter of the mountain, are we even to describe your chin? It has no equal.
lines.272: Your neck, its skin forever roughened with the thrill of Shiva's embrace,
lines.273: carries the beauty of a lotus-stalk, holding up the lotus that is your face;
lines.274: and beneath it, your pearl-necklace — white in itself, yet streaked dark with smeared aloe-wood paste —
lines.275: takes on the delicate look of a lotus-fiber.
lines.276: O you skilled beyond all others in melody, ornament, and song,
lines.277: the three fine lines on your neck shine like a pledge given at your wedding, guaranteeing the true number of well-tuned strings,
lines.278: marking out, as it were, the fixed boundaries
lines.279: of the three registers from which so many sweet melodic modes arise.
lines.280: Brahma, born of the lotus, praises with each of his four mouths
lines.281: the beauty of your four arms, soft and slender as lotus-stalks —
lines.282: as if, fearful of their nails ever since Shiva tore open the demon Andhaka with his own,
lines.283: he offers, from each of his four heads at once, the gesture of fearlessness, pleading to be spared.
lines.284: O Uma, tell me — how are we even to describe the splendor of your hands,
lines.285: whose glowing fingernails mock the color of a freshly opened lotus?
lines.286: The lotus itself could claim even the smallest likeness
lines.287: only if it had first been dyed red by the playful feet of Lakshmi herself.
lines.288: May your two breasts, which nursed Skanda and elephant-faced Ganesha alike,
lines.289: ever flowing at their tips, take away our sorrow, O goddess —
lines.290: breasts at the very sight of which Ganesha's heart, seized by a sudden, comic worry,
lines.291: sends his hand quickly to touch his own two elephant-temples, as if to check.
lines.292: O banner of the mountain-lord's whole house, we have no doubt at all
lines.293: that these two breasts of yours are jeweled vessels brimming with the very nectar of immortality —
lines.294: for the two boys who once drank from them, elephant-faced Ganesha and Skanda who split Mount Krauncha,
lines.295: remain to this day untouched by the company of a wife, forever young.
lines.296: O mother, the full swell of your breasts bears a flawless pearl necklace,
lines.297: its pearls formed in the very foreheads of mighty elephants,
lines.298: its whiteness shot through, within, by the red glow of your bimba-fruit lips —
lines.299: like the very fame of Shiva himself, pure and bright, yet everywhere threaded through with the glow of his fierce valor.
lines.300: O daughter of the mountain, I think your breast-milk is nothing less
lines.301: than the very ocean of Saraswati's own eloquence, flowing straight from your heart —
lines.302: for the child from the south who tasted it, given to him by your own compassion,
lines.303: became, through that alone, a poet cherished among the most accomplished of poets.
lines.304: Kama, his whole body seared by the tongues of flame from Shiva's own wrath,
lines.305: took refuge, O daughter of the mountain, in the deep lake that is your navel;
lines.306: and from there rose a thin trail of smoke —
lines.307: which people, O mother, take simply for the fine line of down that traces your belly.
lines.308: O auspicious mother, that faint, wave-like curve which the wise perceive
lines.309: on your slender waist, resembling the delicate ripples of the Yamuna —
lines.310: it looks as though the very space once pressed thin between your two breasts,
lines.311: were now slipping free and entering the hollow of your navel.
lines.312: Your navel, O daughter of the mountain, is triumphant —
lines.313: a still whirlpool of the Ganga, the very root from which the fine line of down climbing to your breast takes rise, the pit where the fire of Kama's own radiance was once offered up,
lines.314: an indescribable chamber of delight for Rati herself,
lines.315: and the very door to the hidden cave sought after by Shiva's own eye.
lines.316: O jewel among women, your waist — already slender by nature,
lines.317: weighed down further and bowed by the burden of your breasts, seeming almost, slowly, about to break —
lines.318: may it, like a young tree still holding its ground on the crumbling bank of a river,
lines.319: find lasting well-being and stand firm, O daughter of the mountain.
lines.320: O goddess, your two breasts, golden as twin pots, their sides moist at once with sweat, straining against your bodice,
lines.321: press and graze against the base of your arms —
lines.322: and Kama, thinking your waist alone unable to bear their weight without breaking,
lines.323: seems to have bound it three times over, like tendrils of a creeper, to keep it from snapping.
lines.324: O Parvati, your father, the lord of mountains, as though in the very act of giving you in marriage,
lines.325: seems to have taken the weight and breadth of his own slopes and placed them upon you.
lines.326: That is why this vast, weighty swell of your hips now spreads wide enough to cover the whole earth,
lines.327: and, in doing so, leaves the earth itself feeling light by comparison.
lines.328: Having conquered, with your two thighs, both the trunks of great elephants
lines.329: and the smooth golden stalks of plantain trees alike, O daughter of the mountain, knower of every rite,
lines.330: you have, with your two rounded knees — hardened from bowing again and again before your lord —
lines.331: become, as it were, the very twin frontal lobes of the elephant of the gods.
lines.332: In order to conquer Rudra himself, O daughter of the mountain,
lines.333: Kama the archer must surely have turned your two calves into a pair of quivers, each holding twice his usual five arrows —
lines.334: for at the tips of your two feet can be seen ten arrow-points,
lines.335: disguised as toenails, sharpened fine on the very touchstone of the gods' bowed crowns.
lines.336: Place upon my head too, O mother, out of sheer compassion,
lines.337: those same two feet that the crowning heights of scripture themselves bear upon their own heads —
lines.338: feet whose ceremonial washing-water is the very river flowing in Pashupati's matted locks,
lines.339: and whose red lac-dye glows with the same radiance as the crest-jewels on the heads of Vishnu and the other gods.
lines.340: We offer our words of salutation to this pair of your feet,
lines.341: so pleasing to the eye, glowing bright with fresh red lac-dye —
lines.342: feet that even Shiva, lord of all creatures, feels a jealous longing to be struck by,
lines.343: so keenly does the Ashoka tree in your pleasure-garden covet that very touch, said to make it bloom.
lines.344: When your lord, feigning a slip of the tongue, bows his head low in mock shame,
lines.345: you strike him lightly on the forehead with your lotus foot —
lines.346: and at that, the jingling of your anklet-bells bursts out as if in triumphant laughter,
lines.347: as though it had finally drawn out some old, hidden thorn planted long ago by Shiva's rival, the god of love.
lines.348: O mother, your two feet are triumphant over the lotus — and what wonder is that?
lines.349: The lotus withers in the frost, closes and sleeps through the night, and turns clear only in the night's last hour;
lines.350: though it is a fit seat for Lakshmi, it grants prosperity to its devotees only sparingly,
lines.351: while your feet, unlike it, bestow their grace freely, at every hour.
lines.352: O goddess, your foot is itself the very home of fame, and the undoing of every misfortune —
lines.353: how, then, could the wise ever have likened the arch of it to a hard tortoise shell?
lines.354: And how could Shiva himself, destroyer of the triple city, at the hour of your wedding,
lines.355: have taken it in his own two arms and set it down on a mere stone, his heart moved only to compassion?
lines.356: O fierce one, your two feet, through their moon-bright nails that make the lotus-hands of heavenly women close in shame,
lines.357: seem to laugh at the divine wish-granting trees —
lines.358: for those trees only give their fruit, with tender-shoot hands, to the gods who are already wealthy,
lines.359: while your feet bestow auspicious fortune on the poor, freely and at once.
lines.360: That foot of yours, ceaselessly granting fortune to the poor, matching each one's own wish,
lines.361: scatters generously, like pollen, the sheer wealth of its own beauty —
lines.362: may my soul, sinking deep in devotion, every one of its faculties turned into a foot,
lines.363: come at last to rest there, like a bee drawn to a cluster of coral-tree blossoms.
lines.364: O you of lovely conduct, the pet swans that live in your household,
lines.365: stumbling as if only just learning to imitate your own graceful gait, never give up their game —
lines.366: and so your lotus foot, under the pretext of the sweet jingling of its own jeweled anklets,
lines.367: seems to go on teaching them, over and over, exactly how it is done.
lines.368: Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, and Ishvara become the very legs of your couch,
lines.369: and Shiva himself its plank, his own pure, crystal radiance serving as a covering cloth —
lines.370: and reddened all over by the glow reflected from you,
lines.371: the whole scene appears, to delighted eyes, like passion itself given visible, bodily form.
lines.372: Curling in her hair, yet naturally artless in her gentle smile;
lines.373: delicate as a shirisha blossom at heart, yet hard as stone across her breast;
lines.374: exceedingly slender at the waist, yet full and wide where her breasts rise —
lines.375: some indescribable, red-hued compassion of Shiva, taking this very form to save the world, reigns triumphant.
lines.376: The moon's dark mark is really musk, its very orb made of nectar-water;
lines.377: an emerald casket, densely packed with slivers of camphor —
lines.378: and because you draw upon these each day for your own adornment, leaving them empty,
lines.379: Brahma, surely for your sake alone, must keep refilling them, again and again.
lines.380: You are the very inner household of Shiva himself, the enemy of the three cities;
lines.381: that is why the proper rite of worshipping your two feet is not easily granted to those of restless senses.
lines.382: And it is precisely by standing at your doorway, waiting,
lines.383: that Indra and the other gods attained the matchless powers of becoming infinitesimal and the rest.
lines.384: How many poets have not won Saraswati, Brahma's own wife, as their muse?
lines.385: And who, with wealth of one kind or another, does not become some sort of husband to Lakshmi?
lines.386: But you, most faithful of faithful wives, grant the mere touch of your breasts to no one but Shiva himself —
lines.387: not even to the kurabaka tree, said to bloom only at a lovely woman's touch.
lines.388: Those versed in scripture speak of three: the goddess of speech, wife of Brahma;
lines.389: Padma, wife of Vishnu; and the daughter of the mountain, companion of Shiva.
lines.390: But you are a fourth, beyond them, an indescribable glory without limit —
lines.391: O queen of the Supreme Brahman, great power of illusion, you alone set the whole universe turning.
lines.392: O mother, tell me — when, as a seeker of knowledge,
lines.393: shall I get to drink the water that has washed your feet, tinged red with their own lac-dye?
lines.394: That water which is itself the very cause of poetry, even in those born naturally mute —
lines.395: when will it come to taste, in my own mouth, like betel-juice from the lotus-mouth of Saraswati?
lines.396: Whoever worships you comes to rival Brahma and Vishnu themselves,
lines.397: sporting with Saraswati and Lakshmi both his own, his beauty of form even loosening Rati's devotion to her own husband.
lines.398: Freed, even while still living, from the whole tangle of worldly bondage,
lines.399: he goes on, through a long life, tasting that flavor known as the supreme bliss.
lines.400: To wave a lamp's small flame before the sun is an empty gesture;
lines.401: to offer the moon, source of nectar, a few drops drawn from a moonstone is no less futile;
lines.402: to satisfy the ocean with water taken from its own depths achieves nothing —
lines.403: just so, O mother, is this hymn of praise to your powers of speech, offered back to you in words that are themselves your own gift.
lines.404: This Soundarya Lahari is the foremost of hymns, the bringer of good fortune,
lines.405: composed by the venerable teacher himself — whoever recites it attains liberation.
lines.406: Thus ends the hymn composed by the venerable teacher, the wandering renunciant of the highest order,
lines.407: disciple of the venerable and worshipful Govinda Bhagavatpada —
lines.408: the venerable Shankara Bhagavatpada. Here the Soundarya Lahari is complete.
lines.411: Brought, by the touch of your two feet, to become a jeweled mirror —
lines.412: the very jewel of the sky, the moon, its rays grown soft and hushed within, as if out of fear —
lines.413: (A variant reading gives this differently: soft and still, rather than hushed within out of fear.)
lines.414: holds the reflection of your face, ever-blooming there, without pause,
lines.415: untroubled, calm, as though it were the very lotus of its own heart.
lines.416: O Uma, some of your devotees, in the purity of their meditation,
lines.417: picture a form with a chest swelling under full breasts, a lovely smile, a touch of Kama's own playfulness in its sidelong glance, a body radiant as the kadamba blossom —
lines.418: a form so like you that it confuses even Shiva himself into mistaking it for you,
lines.419: (Variant readings differ here, naming Kama as the one who creates this confusion, or describing the form as matching or surpassing your own beauty.)
lines.420: and this very confusion it creates in Shiva's mind is the fruit that ripens for such devotees.
lines.421: O treasure, ever-smiling one, of boundless virtue, skilled in right conduct,
lines.422: of unshakeable wisdom, the sole dwelling place of minds given over to discipline,
lines.423: free from the bonds of fate, the very being praised at the culmination of all scripture,
lines.424: fearless one, eternal one — accept this small hymn of mine as well.
